paragraphs.text: Semantic code search for DeepSeek Harness: the Semble index as two native MCP tools (search / find_r
elated), so an agent finds code by behaviour instead of guessing file names.
dsh-semble
English | 简体中文

`dsh-semble` brings Semble — a code search engine built for
agents — into each DSH session as two na

tive tools: `semble_search` and `semble_find_related`. Since
3.0.0 there is no MCP layer: the plugin

registers the tools directly into the host's tool registry,
and every call spawns the Semble CLI th

rough `uvx`. `grep` needs a
string you already know; this needs a description of behaviour — "where

is the retry policy applied
when a request fails", "which module decides the scoring weights". That

is usually the moment an
agent starts guessing file names. And because only the matched snippets com

e back instead of whole
files, one query costs a fraction of the tokens of a grep-then-read detour:

upstream benchmarks
measure **~99% fewer tokens** than grep+read, at retrieval quality on par with c

ode-specialized
transformer retrievers.

Under the hood, Semble splits every file into code-aware chunks with tree-sitter, then retrieves
aga

inst two complementary signals: static **Model2Vec** embeddings (the code-specialized
`potion-code-1

6M-v2` model) for semantic similarity, and **BM25** for lexical matches on identifiers
and API names

. The two result lists are fused with **Reciprocal Rank Fusion** (RRF), then re-ranked
by code-aware

signals: a chunk that *defines* the queried symbol outranks one that merely mentions
it, query word

s matching identifier stems inside a chunk earn extra weight (`parse config →
parseConfig / config_p

arser`), several hits from the same file promote the file as a whole, and
test files, examples and c

ompat shims are demoted so the canonical implementation surfaces first.
[该节后续省略]
## What you get
| Tool | Hand it | Back comes |
| `semble_search` | a sentence describing the code or where it lives | ranked `file:line` hits with

snippets |
| `semble_find_related` | one location you already know | its neighbours: other implement
ations, callers, tests |

The bundle also registers one slash command, `/semble`, for the reporting subcommands the tools do
n

ot expose: `/semble savings`, `/semble file-types`, `/semble version` and
`/semble clear <index|savi

ngs|orphans|all>`. See
Commands.
A typical exchange:

> **You:** Where does DSH decide that a plugin is "loaded"?
>
> **Agent:** calls `semble_search`, ge

ts a hit in the plugin inventory, opens it with `read`, finds
> `isEntryLoaded` comparing loader ent

ry names against the package name, and answers from the source
> rather than from a guess.
## Using the tools
- `repo` — **required**. Absolute path of the repository, or an `https://` git URL. A list searches

several repositories at once.
- `top_k` — default 5. Raise to 10–20 when the first pass misses.
- `m

ax_snippet_lines` — default 10; `0` returns locations only.
- `content` — `code` (default), `docs`,

default 10; `0` returns locations only.
- `content` — `code` (default), `docs`, `config`, or `all`.

The first query against a repository builds its index (slow, one-time); later queries reuse it.
Hits

are ranked by similarity. Search scores are rank-fusion values that stay small (`0.0x`) even
for ex

actly-relevant code — treat them as a relative ordering, not an absolute confidence. An
*empty* resu
lt is the real "nothing relevant here" signal.

and lock

### Prerequisites
uv must be on PATH — `uvx` launches Semble from PyPI:

First start downloads the package and the embedding model (~1–2 min, one-time, offline afterwards).
Restart DSH once after installing; until then the settings row may read 待重启.
## Compatibility
The package follows semver. The public surface, which 3.x keeps stable:

- the two native tools `semble_search` and `semble_find_related` (their behavior tracks the
PyPI `se

mble` release uvx resolves — the plugin pins nothing, see *How it is wired*);
- the plugin entry: th

e default export and the named `apply` from `dsh-semble`, receiving
`(ctx, config)` — `config` is th

e loader row's `config`, coerced by the plugin; the context
carries `skills` and optionally `inject`

/`tools`/`commands`;
- the `/semble` subcommand allow-list (`savings`, `file-types`, `version`) and
and `./package.json`.

Not covered by the promise: row ids and launch details inside `cordis.patch.yml` (they are host
wiri

ng, not API), the routing skill's name and body, and everything under `lib/` except the entry
point

— tests may import `parseSembleArgs`/`runSemble`, but downstream packages should not.
The default `e

ngines` requirement (`node` and `dsh`) only widens within a major version; a raised
minimum is a min
or bump at most, since installs resolve through the package manager.

**2.x → 3.0.0**: the MCP bridge is gone. The tools are renamed from
`mcp__semble__search` / `mcp__se

mble__find_related` to `semble_search` / `semble_find_related`, and
the `toolCallTimeoutMs` setting

becomes `toolTimeoutMs`. The old names are no longer registered;
update any script that referenced t
hem. Restart DSH once after upgrading.

**3.0.0 → 3.0.1**: fixes a load failure on real hosts — the default export did not carry the
`inject

` declaration, so the loader could not see the skill dependency, the plugin row reported as
failed,

and no tools appeared (the 2.x anchor row had the same latent defect; the MCP row was doing
the actu
al work, which hid it). No API changes in 3.0.1; update straight from 3.0.0.
**3.0.1 → 3.0.2**: `/semble` gains the `clear` subcommand (`index` / `savings` / `orphans` / `all`)

so the index cache can be dropped from within a session; the target word is required, and a bare
`/s
emble clear` only prints the usage.
